links.outcome: Classifier performance on external data not used in training or internal validation
links.effect: Repeatability carried over to EXT without retraining (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2-0.4); strong classification performance on EXT required retraining (4.0% extreme misclassifications with n=26 EXT individuals added).
links.quote: Our results indicate strong repeatability of our multiclass model utilizing Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout, which carries over well to “EXT” (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2 - 0.4) even in the absence of retraining, as well as strong classification performance of our model on “EXT” that is achieved with retraining (% extreme misclassifications = 4.0% for n = 26 “EXT” individuals added to “SEED” in a 2n normal : 2n indeterminate : n precancer+ ratio), and incremental improvement of performance following retraining with images from additional individuals.

links.outcome: Repeatability of predictions on repeat images from same patient under identical conditions
links.effect: Strong repeatability with MC dropout, carried over to external data even without retraining (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2-0.4).
links.quote: Our results indicate strong repeatability of our multiclass model utilizing Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout, which carries over well to “EXT” (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2 - 0.4) even in the absence of retraining, as well as strong classification performance of our model on “EXT” that is achieved with retraining (% extreme misclassifications = 4.0% for n = 26 “EXT” individuals added to “SEED” in a 2n normal : 2n indeterminate : n precancer+ ratio), and incremental improvement of performance following retraining with images from additional individuals.

links.outcome: Classification performance on external data after retraining with local samples
links.effect: Retraining with EXT images achieved strong performance (4.0% extreme misclassifications with n=26 EXT individuals added to SEED) with incremental improvement as more individuals were added.
links.quote: Our results indicate strong repeatability of our multiclass model utilizing Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout, which carries over well to “EXT” (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2 - 0.4) even in the absence of retraining, as well as strong classification performance of our model on “EXT” that is achieved with retraining (% extreme misclassifications = 4.0% for n = 26 “EXT” individuals added to “SEED” in a 2n normal : 2n indeterminate : n precancer+ ratio), and incremental improvement of performance following retraining with images from additional individuals.

links.outcome: Model performance variation across image capture device and geography
links.effect: Device-level heterogeneity affected model performance more than geography-level heterogeneity.
links.quote: We additionally find that device-level heterogeneity affects our model performance more than geography-level heterogeneity.
